          # baseRanges + per-file alignment. Without it the server suppresses the
          # findings, because a protocol-1 diff cannot be trusted.
          # Write the body to a file rather than passing it as an argument.
          # docs[] carries whole spec files, and Linux caps a SINGLE argument at

            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${LORE_INGEST_TOKEN}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            --data-binary @impact-body.json \
            "${LORE_INGEST_URL}/api/repos/${{ github.repository }}/impact" || echo 000)

          case "$CODE" in
            2*) ;;
            401|403) REASON="Lore rejected the request ($CODE) - the LORE_INGEST_TOKEN secret is missing, expired, or lacks the write scope." ;;
            404) REASON="Lore has no impact endpoint for this repo ($CODE) - it may not be onboarded yet." ;;
            *)   REASON="Lore API unreachable (HTTP $CODE). This check could not run." ;;

            node -e '
              const fs = require("fs");
              const reason = process.argv[1];
              fs.writeFileSync("impact.json", JSON.stringify({
                status: "unavailable", statements: [], orphaned: [], annotations: [],
                comment: "## Lore Spec Impact\n\n" + reason + "\n\n<!-- lore-trace-impact -->",

            let report;
            try { report = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('impact.json', 'utf8')); }
            catch { report = { status: 'unavailable', annotations: [], comment: '## Lore Spec Impact\n\nThis check produced no readable result.\n\n' + MARKER }; }

            // checks:write scope (GITHUB_TOKEN read-only) can never suppress it.
            // Best-effort like the check-run below: pull-requests:write can be
            // denied too, and an advisory check must not fail the PR over it.
            try {

                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.payload.pull_request.number,

              if (existing) {
                await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                  owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, comment_id: existing.id, body,
                });
              } else {
                await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                  owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, issue_number: context.payload.pull_request.number, body,
                });
              }
            } catch (err) {
              core.warning('sticky comment failed (' + err.status + '): grant GITHUB_TOKEN pull-requests:write to enable it.');
            }

            // The annotated check-run is a nice-to-have; best-effort so a 401/403
            // on checks:write logs a warning instead of failing the whole job.
            try {
              const annotations = (report.annotations || []).slice(0, 50);
              await github.rest.checks.create({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                name: 'Lore Spec Impact',
                head_sha: context.payload.pull_request.head.sha,
                status: 'completed',
                conclusion: 'neutral',
                output: {
                  title: 'Lore Spec Impact (advisory)',
                  summary: report.comment || 'No spec impact.',
                  annotations,
                },
              });
            } catch (err) {
              core.warning('checks.create failed (' + err.status + '): grant GITHUB_TOKEN checks:write to enable inline annotations. Sticky comment was still posted.');
            }

**Score:** 1.000

## Problem Statement

Every E4 issue lands in this repository: the TMS client, the tool contract, the auth spike, the chat wiring, the Danish prompt and the escalation path. None of them is meant to carry repo scaffolding, so the scaffolding is built once, here. The PoC target is deliberately narrow, per the client: a simple chat interface that answers questions using tools that call the TMS system. This feature builds the shell that holds it, and answers no question itself.

The repository is also the first honest test of the two published libraries. The epic's M1 exit bar is both packages installing from npm into a third project that has never seen either source repo. Earlier fixtures proved each tarball alone; this is where they arrive together in an application, from the public registry.

Two things are decided that were not when the skeleton was opened. The TMS API is delivered (spec snapshotted at `api/tms-openapi.json`, with endpoint, scope and boundary tables in `api/README.md`). The login approach is settled: the support agent reuses CFOAgent's Clerk-based login, so `auth.ws` validates a Clerk session and its `WsAuthenticator` returns the authenticated user together with the org whose `customerNumber` scopes every later tool call, mirroring CFOAgent's identity and organisation-context layering.

Onboarding the repo into Lore made context assembly work, but nothing created `.lore/test-commands.yml`, the file `lore_list_tests` and `lore_run_test` read, so an agent claiming a pipeline task here could assemble context and could not run a test. The gap was already load-bearing: the browser check in [support-agent-chat](../support-agent-chat/spec.md) (#156) has a criterion that adds an entry to this file, and would otherwise be the first issue in the backlog to touch a file nobody creates.

Lore's first test ingest for this repo (`lore-tests.yml`, run 34584461763 attempt 2, `main@579d822`) then surfaced two defects:

- **No coverage (#220).** Lore projected 16 `TestChunk` nodes and 4 `Coverage` nodes, but not one `Coverage.covers` edge, so every test is recorded as covering nothing. "Which tests cover `apps/api/src/configuration/config.ts`" answers `[]`, and `tdd-round`/`fix-ci` cannot use the graph for this repo. For `coverage_format: lcov`, `lore-code-trace` parses the lcov report from the run command's stdout (`apps/lore-code-trace/report.go`, `runOneFile`: `parseLcovCoverage(string(out))`). `scripts/lore-run-test.mjs` runs vitest with `--coverage.reporter=lcov`, which writes `coverage/lcov.info` to disk, while stdout carries only the `--reporter=verbose` text, so the parser finds no `SF:` records. Until re-cinq/lore#2026 (merged 2026-09-11) that empty list serialised as `"covered": null` and failed the whole report with a 500; it now ingests cleanly as "no coverage", which is why the defect went from loud to silent.
- **Workspace-relative paths (#221).** Lore's graph holds this repo's tests under `test/auth.test.ts`, `test/config.test.ts`, `test/health.test.ts` and `test/logger.test.ts` (Dgraph `TestChunk.file_path`, `main@579d822`), while the files live at `apps/api/test/…`. Nothing in Lore that keys on a repo path (the trace-impact check on PRs, `tests-covering`, spec `validated by` links) can match them. `scripts/lore-list-tests.mjs` computes `file` as `relative(process.cwd(), suite.name)`, relative to the workspace. Lore's contract (`specs/project-test-interface/contracts/test-commands.md`) requires `file` to be a repo-relative path after `path_prefix_strip` and puts the rebasing on the command; `lore-code-trace` only strips `path_prefix_strip` and never prepends `cwd` (`apps/lore-code-trace/report.go:84`). The lcov `SF:` paths need the same rebasing.

- **Settled - the erasure primitive.** #23 made `eraseConversation` the GDPR erasure primitive and said `SessionStore.delete` is not, recording that this contradicts a criterion elsewhere naming `SessionStore.delete` as the primitive. #152 corrects it: "after this merges, it is", once HAL Engine's `hal-engine-session-lifetime` (#117) stops calling `delete` on close. FR-011 states both sides of that engine boundary. #152's requirement to rewrite the #23 spec file becomes CR-009, since this feature spec replaces that file.

- **Settled - synchronous vs awaitable store.** #23 requires the shipped signatures and puts making `SessionStore` asynchronous out of scope; #152 types `delete` as `Promise<boolean>` against HAL Engine's `hal-engine-awaitable-session-store` (#102). - **Settled - the primitive has no caller.** #152 FR-011 stated that nothing in the product calls `store.delete`. #195 replaces it with the erasure use case (FR-058). ([validated by `erases all of a user's data across stores and leaves audit rows unlinked`](../../apps/api/test/erasure.acceptance.test.ts#L30))
- **Settled - two `createdAt` stamps.** #23 stamps `createdAt` on the persisted row and puts adding `ChatSession.createdAt` to the engine out of scope as unnecessary for whole-conversation retention. #194 has `create` stamp `ChatSession.createdAt`, a field HAL Engine's `hal-engine-session-age-fields` (#106) adds upstream, for the cache's age bound. - **Settled - the sweep as built (#297).** #23's port and `PersistentSessionStore` were not built (#23 closed as not planned): HAL Engine's `MongoSessionStore` owns both the cache and the documents, and since 0.7.0 its `eraseOlderThan` pages the expired ids, deletes them and drops exactly those from the cache. The sweep lives in `apps/api/src/conversations/retentionSweep.ts`, beside the store, rather than FR-021's `apps/api/src/sessions/retention.ts`, and #297's `apps/api/src/sessions/retentionSweep.ts`: no `sessions/` directory exists. - **Open - reading the cache count.** CR-011 and FR-033 observe the cache count, while CR-010 forbids any public member beyond the five `SessionStore` methods. #194 does not say how a test reads the count without such a member; it is left to the plan.

## Lint guardrails

Codified house conventions, enforced by one repo-local plugin loaded by
relative import in `eslint.config.mjs` (no package.json, no build, no
publish), `tools/eslint-plugin-bowman/` for this repo's own rules, by the
published `@re-cinq/eslint-plugin-re-lint` package for re-cinq's generic
rules (decision 9), plus a handful of core-ESLint entries (decisions 1-7). Those are validated against committed
fixtures by `tests/eslint-house-rules.test.ts`, judged by the exact committed
config via `--no-ignore` (the same mechanism the Labels and duplication
fixtures use). Decision 8's third-party `react-hooks` rules carry no such
fixture: they are validated by the three exempt components' own behavioural
tests.

Decisions:

1. **Named exports only in `src/`.** The public surface is `export const`,
   so a rename is a compile error in every consumer instead of a silent
   aliasing. Enforced as an `ExportDefaultDeclaration` selector that rides
   in every `no-restricted-syntax` overlay - a later overlay replaces the
   whole array, so the selector is spread into each one rather than added as
   a fourth object.
2. **A condition chains at most two boolean operators at the sites where
   conditions live inline** (`bowman/max-boolean-operators`): `if`/loop
   tests, ternaries, JSX conditional renders, variable initialisers and
   assignments. Anything denser is lifted into a named predicate -
   `isCopyChord` and `hasModifier` in `ChatMessage.tsx` are the founding
   examples. Return statements and arrow-function bodies are deliberately
   NOT counted: they are where the named predicate lives, and the name is
   the fix - counting them would put the extraction itself over budget
   (`isCopyChord` legally chains four operators for exactly this reason).
   The accepted cost: a dense return inside a vaguely-named function passes,
   and the function name is the reviewable surface there. `??` is
   value-selection, not branching, and never counts.
3. **No catch-as-control-flow** (`bowman/no-catch-as-control-flow`). A catch
   that swallows the error and fabricates a return value from a call is an
   `if` in disguise. Sentinel fallbacks (`catch { return null; }`) stay
   legal.
4. **No network egress in component code** (`bowman/no-network-egress`). The
   privacy contract is enforced at runtime by the `tests/setup.ts` traps and
   at the dependency level by `scripts/check-forbidden-imports.mjs`; the
   lint rule is the review-time backstop that names the violation before a
   test ever runs. Denylisted channels: `fetch` (bare or via
   window/globalThis/self), `new WebSocket/EventSource/XMLHttpRequest`,
   `navigator.sendBeacon`.
5. **Props are read-only** (`bowman/no-prop-mutation`). Data flows down as
   arguments; changes flow up via callback props. Scope-based, so a local
   sharing a prop's name never trips it; only the first parameter is props,
   leaving a `forwardRef` second argument and its `.current` writes alone.
6. **Styling lives in the stylesheet** (`re-lint/no-inline-styles`), with one
   passing shape - an object of nothing but CSS custom properties, because
   the styling rules then still live in the stylesheet reading the variable.
   The rule is the package's since 2026-09-08: bowman's own port existed only
   because lore's fired under a hardcoded `/apps/web-ui/` path marker, and
   re-lint 1.0 replaced that with a `files` scope; the committed fixtures
   then proved the package's copy catches the computed-width violation,
   passes the custom-properties-only object, and over `src/` fires on nothing
   but the two exempt components, so the port was deleted.
   Two components are exempted by path in `eslint.config.mjs`, each a
   recorded decision asserted by its tests, not tolerated drift:
   `ConversationList` (the per-character typewriter animation is data, one
   opacity per character) and `ThinkingDots` (the per-dot stagger is data,
   one delay per dot). Visually hidden text is one stylesheet rule,
   `.bowman-sr-only` in `src/styles.css`, shared by the markdown notice, the
   `Toast` live region, `ConversationList`'s plain title and
   `useFocusGroups`' announcement region; issue 5 retired the three inline
   copies and with them the "works with no consumer stylesheet" argument,
   since README already requires `./styles.css` of every consumer. The one
   other hiding idiom is `AppShell`'s skip link, which uses Tailwind's
   `sr-only` with `focus:not-sr-only` because it must become visible on
   focus. `tests/styles.test.ts` fails on a hand-written clip literal in `src/`
   and on the stylesheet losing the rule.
7. **House style is autofixable and repo-wide**: `curly` ("all") plus
   `@stylistic/padding-line-between-statements` (blank line before returns
   and control flow, after the import block and declaration groups).
   Prettier neither inserts nor removes single blank lines between
   statements, so `eslint --fix` followed by `prettier --write` reaches a
   fixed point. Pinned like every other guardrail: the house-style fixture
   in `tests/eslint-house-rules.test.ts` fails with both rule ids.
8. **`react-hooks`'s `refs` and `set-state-in-effect`.** The
   recommended-latest set fires exactly six times, all at three documented,
   test-asserted render patterns and nowhere else, so the two rules are
   adopted and those three sites are exempted by path in `eslint.config.mjs`,
   each a recorded decision rather than tolerated drift: `ChatMessage`'s
   monotonic entry-id thinking-indicator latch (a ref read and written during
   render, keyed by `entry.id` and idempotent) and `useSidebarState`'s
   `storedOpenRef` latest-value read are exempted from `refs`; `Toast`'s
   empty-then-filled live region, seeded in a mount effect so its text is
   reliably announced, is exempted from `set-state-in-effect`. As with
   decision 6 the exemption is file-wide, the accepted cost being that a
   genuinely unsafe ref or effect later added to one of these three files
   would pass.

9. **The generic subset of re-cinq's lint rules comes from the published
   `@re-cinq/eslint-plugin-re-lint` package.** It is the home lore's plugin
   was extracted into on 2026-09-08 (re-cinq/re-lint, Apache-2.0, built and

## Lint guardrails

Codified house conventions, enforced by one repo-local plugin loaded by
relative import in `eslint.config.mjs` (no package.json, no build, no

Decisions:

1. **Named exports only in `src/`.** The public surface is `export const`,
   so a rename is a compile error in every consumer instead of a silent
   aliasing. Enforced as an `ExportDefaultDeclaration` selector that rides
   in every `no-restricted-syntax` overlay - a later overlay replaces the
   whole array, so the selector is spread into each one rather than added as
   a fourth object.
2. **A condition chains at most two boolean operators at the sites where
   conditions live inline** (`bowman/max-boolean-operators`): `if`/loop
   tests, ternaries, JSX conditional renders, variable initialisers and
   assignments. Anything denser is lifted into a named predicate -
   `isCopyChord` and `hasModifier` in `ChatMessage.tsx` are the founding
   examples. Return statements and arrow-function bodies are deliberately
   NOT counted: they are where the named predicate lives, and the name is
   the fix - counting them would put the extraction itself over budget
   (`isCopyChord` legally chains four operators for exactly this reason).
   The accepted cost: a dense return inside a vaguely-named function passes,
   and the function name is the reviewable surface there. `??` is
   value-selection, not branching, and never counts.
3. **No catch-as-control-flow** (`bowman/no-catch-as-control-flow`). A catch
   that swallows the error and fabricates a return value from a call is an
   `if` in disguise. Sentinel fallbacks (`catch { return null; }`) stay
   legal.
4. **No network egress in component code** (`bowman/no-network-egress`). The
   privacy contract is enforced at runtime by the `tests/setup.ts` traps and
   at the dependency level by `scripts/check-forbidden-imports.mjs`; the

   library ships no such helper, and `src/` carries no `throw` at all after

   rewrites a dead link as faithfully as a live one. Its one recorded

    agreement, `scripts/check-spec-links.mjs` imports `segmentStatements` and

    of lore's `libs/shared/src` domain, so the local verdict is lore's own by
    construction. It is the local counterpart of lore's spec-coverage-validate
    job: one line per misplaced citation, a `misplaced: N across M specs`
    summary, exit 1 on any finding. Until 2026-09-08 the domain was a
    byte-exact mirror of lore's TypeScript under `tools/lore-shared/`, run
    under `--experimental-strip-types` behind a module-resolve hook that
    mapped lore's `.js` specifiers onto the `.ts` files; the package ships
    built JavaScript, so the hook, the flag and the Node 22.6 floor it
    implied are gone.

    keeps what a rule cannot express.** Issue 17 asks for three lint-time
    checks over `specs/**/spec.md` and `adrs/**`: every testable statement
    carries a trailing `([validated by](...))` link, every doc opens with a
    lead paragraph, and every doc declares a lifecycle status its own link
    coverage entitles it to claim. The package ships all three as rules.
    `re-lint/require-intro-paragraph` runs at error over `specs/**/spec.md`
    and `adrs/*.md`, and `re-lint/require-status-matches-coverage` over

    `--coverage` reports the unlinked statements.

      across the corpus carried no link when this landed, and the repo lints
      at zero warnings, so `require-statement-links` stays off (a `warn`
      would be red under `--max-warnings 0`). The count lives behind
      `--coverage`, which lists every unlinked statement and always exits 0;
      the backfill is the sweep tasks' work, and turning it red on day one
      would only mean disabling it.

      folds `accepted` into `shipped`, so an ADR carrying `status: accepted`
      and no test links would be demanded to link every statement it makes -
      the wrong ask of a decision record. The tier rule is therefore scoped
      to specs by its `files` glob, and the script carries the ADR half the
      rule would otherwise have given for free: a parseable status.

    they imported an unpublished shared package, their pure parts
    were mirrored under `tools/lore-shared/` and
    `tools/eslint-plugin-lore/rules/lib/` behind a local shim, and the script
    held all three verdicts. The package vendors that domain, so the rules
    run as rules.

    4% ceiling over `src` and `tests`, which a bare `npx jscpd .` showed to be
    a gate over the wrong scope: `src/` had no clones at all, while the same
    six routines were hand-copied across the test suites (source-hygiene
    assertions, built-file directive and pack checks, script runners, ESLint
    fixture linting, focus-environment stubs), two scripts each carried their
    own `listSourceFiles`, and the workflow jobs repeated one setup block. The
    copies now live once, in `tests/helpers/`, `scripts/lib/` and the
    `setup-node-install` composite action (issue 157 later folded three more
    directory walks and the Lore scripts' Vitest report runner into the same
    homes), and the gate holds the tree there:
    `path` is the repo, `threshold` is 0, and a red check is fixed only by
    extracting a helper. Three inputs are ignored because they are not code
    and cannot be deduplicated: `**/package-lock.json` (generated, the same
    packages resolved in three trees), `**/*.md` (jscpd's markdown tokenizer

  contradicts the test architecture.

  upstreaming those three detections and then retiring the ports is the
  eventual fix. `no-inline-styles` passed the same probe and moved
